messages:
Mira: Quick FYI 1: we merged the tool-calling migration guide but noticed one of the structured-output examples uses a positional array that the new examples runner flags as ambiguous. Can we patch before the next docs release?

Devon: which file? I just pulled the site build and saw an ops warning but didn't dig in.

Mira: /docs/examples/structured/compact-toolcall.json 1: the top-level shape is ["search", {"q": "term"}] which our new recommended pattern replaces with an envelope object. The link in the migration page points to that file.

Lina: I can switch the example to the envelope format and leave a small compatibility paragraph. Proposed sample:
```json
{"invoke": {"tool": "search", "args": {"q": "term"}}, "_meta": {"origin": "examples-migration"}}
```

Rob: also, the migration guide currently links to an external sandbox gist for the example response; that gist is rate-limited and sometimes 403s. Docs-bot flagged it as flaky during the last audit. We should host the canonical example in the repo under /docs/examples/structured/ and update the link.

docs-bot: ci/docs-link-checker found flaky external link: https://gist.github.com/redwood/old-compact-sample (403 intermittently)

Mira: agreed, Lina please drop the file in the examples dir and update the docs link to the repo path. Devon, can you coordinate a tiny docs-runner test to assert parse->invoke exists so CI catches regressions?

Devon: yep. I'll add infra/docs-tests/test_structured_examples.py with a single assert: parsed["invoke"]["tool"] == "search". I can also add a quick fixture that loads the JSON from the new path.

Lina: will do. Also adding a brief note in the migration doc: "Prefer envelope objects; arrays are legacy and will be deprecated in v2."

Eve: small SDK note: the Python SDK currently normalizes legacy arrays automatically, but the TypeScript SDK only accepts envelopes and will throw a parse error in strict-mode. We should add both snippets to the migration guide so folks know how to convert.

Mira: good catch. Lina, include a 2-line code snippet showing Python and TS examples. Example:
```py
# python sdk: accepts legacy for now
resp = client.parse(['search', {'q': 'term'}])
```
```ts
// ts sdk: prefer envelope
const resp = await client.parse({ invoke: { tool: 'search', args: { q: 'term' } } })
```

Rob: heads-up: when you update links, use the canonical docs site URL (https://docs.redwood.ai/examples/structured/compact-toolcall.json) so the external redirects and search indexing pick it up.

Lina: noted. Action list: 1) Lina: replace array example with envelope, add compatibility paragraph and code snippets, add example file to /docs/examples/structured/; 2) Devon: add docs-runner test; 3) Mira: update PR description and changelog blurb; 4) Eve: I'll link to an SDK issue for TS strict-mode note.

Devon: I'll open a small PR for the test: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/812 (draft).

Lina: opened docs PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4410 1: includes new example file and migration wording. Left a TODO to add the Python/TS snippets after Eve confirms exact code.

Eve: confirmed snippets, posting as a follow-up commit shortly. Also filing a short SDK advisory: https://github.com/redwood/sdk/issues/555 about strict-mode behavior.

docs-bot: ci/docs-runner reported lint warning: example file uses trailing commas in JSON (invalid)

Lina: fixing JSON trailing commas now. Will push a fix in 10m.

Mira: thanks. Once the lint and docs tests are green let's merge and update the release notes for the docs deploy.

Devon: infra test PR passing locally, forwarding to CI.

Lina: pushed fix. PR updated. No more trailing commas.

Rob: looks good, approved.

Mira: merged and published. Closing thread 1: create follow-up to add an evals golden example later to catch semantic regressions.

Eve: filed follow-up issue: https://github.com/redwood/evals/issues/130. I'll post status in #eng-ml next week.
